title: The TRUTH About the Software Development Job Market in 2026
summary: Data-driven argument that SWE job postings are recovering and Jevons paradox favors developers.

assertions.quote: listings for software engineers on Indeed are up 11% annually

verdicts.note: Postings rose from the 2023 trough in some trackers (TrueUp, parts of Indeed), but remain far below 2022 and junior postings stayed weak; the data are mixed.

assertions.quote: this was kind of just a coincidence ... a combination of economic factors

verdicts.note: The 2022-23 decline began before ChatGPT and tracks rate hikes and over-hiring; most economists attribute it mainly to macro factors, though AI may weigh on junior roles since 2024.

assertions.quote: making something more efficient often increases total consumption of that thing

verdicts.note: Jevons effects are historically common and plausible for software, but whether demand growth outpaces productivity for developer headcount is unproven.

assertions.quote: they need you to believe that so that they can then raise an even bigger round of funding

verdicts.note: Labs do have incentives and many evals are self-reported, but independent evals (METR, SWE-bench, LMArena) largely confirm capability gains.

assertions.quote: 41% ... of all the code being written by the biggest companies in the world is currently being written by AI

verdicts.note: Google and Microsoft executives cite ~25-50% of new code AI-generated; the figures are self-reported and usually count accepted suggestions, not finished code.

assertions.quote: instead of AI replacing programmers, the nature of the job simply changes

verdicts.note: Through 2026 evidence points to role change and slower junior hiring, not elimination of the profession; long-run is uncertain.
